title: Symmetric networks of loops persist at every size; where a loop meets a shared ring they cannot
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In networks of rule-60 rings a contact keeps its witnesses at every lag exactly when its returns cancel; a symmetry exchanging a contact's two rings cancels them, so loops, two rings sharing contacts, the Platonic networks and square, triangular and honeycomb lattices on a torus persist at every size. Where a two-contact ring meets a larger ring, one return of length 2 is unpaired and the witnesses lapse, as in every figure-eight and chord across a loop.
